source.title: Explainable LLM Unlearning Through Reasoning
source.authors: Junfeng Liao; Qi-Zhou Wang; Shan-Shan Ye; Xing-Tong Yu; Ling Chen; Zhen Fang

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether cross-lingual prompts, jailbreaks, and small fine-tuning attacks undo unlearning, using a new reasoning-based method and LLM-as-a-Judge measures.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports main benchmark and retention results, but its attack experiments directly relevant here are the cross-lingual, jailbreak, and relearning results below. It does not test activation-direction ablation or quantization. The cited prior-work results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study proposes a new unlearning method (TRU) and claims it resists cross-lingual, jailbreak and small relearning attacks on WMDP-Bio, which bears on F and indirectly on B and E. Robustness is measured only with an LLM-judged composite score (UQ: relevance, rejection, helpfulness), not with recovered-knowledge accuracy.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude TRU gives controlled, explainable unlearning with refusals while preserving general ability. They report it as robust to cross-lingual, jailbreak and small relearning attacks, with only slight UQ drops. Note that this robustness is measured solely by the LLM-judged UQ score, not by recovered accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: TRU combines supervised training on generated reasoning-and-refusal targets with a gradient-ascent-based loss; it is a new method rather than a reproduction of the cited unlearning methods.
record.method_sensitivity: UQ changes across attack conditions: the reported decreases are 0.24 for Spanish, 0.47 for Russian, 0.33 and 0.65 for the two jailbreak prompts, and 0.45 and 0.39 for the two relearning settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Moving the correct option from A to D raises MCQ-based 'unlearning performance' sharply (GradDiff 76.0→100). The authors attribute this to option-position bias in collapsed models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Near-chance WMDP accuracy after unlearning can be an artifact of answer-position bias rather than knowledge erasure.

record.problems: Attack robustness is assessed with LLM-as-a-Judge UQ rather than direct measurement of recovered factual knowledge. The attack results are reported without uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant attack-result rows were omitted.

untested.parts: Post-attack WMDP accuracy is not measured. Pre-attack accuracy appears only in Table 7, with no base-model row.
Relearning on unrelated or loosely related data; larger or longer relearning budgets; accuracy-based recovery.
No activation-direction ablation or representation analysis.
No plain rephrasing, in-context information or adversarial prompt search. Only two fixed jailbreak prompts and two languages were tried.
Resistance to quantization, internal edits, stronger relearning, and evaluation by accuracy rather than a judge score.

missing.what: Standard metrics for TRU (no attack). WMDP column 0.6732 Bio and 0.7106 Cyber, apparently 1−accuracy, i.e. ~33%/29% accuracy vs 25% chance. MMLU is 0.4577/0.4399 vs RMU 0.571. The column definition is unclear and no base-model row is given.
Qualitative case studies claiming Spanish translations of in-scope prompts elicit knowledge from NPO, RMU and WGA. The shown outputs are off-topic text rather than the targeted facts.
GSM8K retention after TOFU-Forget05: TRU 0.423, RMU 0.471, NPO 0.441, GA 0.002.

record.verdict_notes: The reader used invalid version codes (V2/V5/V6); these were remapped to B/E/F. Changed row states from absent to partial: each attack moves UQ down somewhat and there is no uncertainty to call it negligible. TRU is essentially refusal-plus-reasoning SFT combined with GradDiff, and UQ rewards refusal style. A UQ drop does not equal knowledge recovery, and an unchanged UQ does not prove the knowledge is gone. The relearning attacks are far weaker than those in Lynch et al. or later relearning studies.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not establish that targeted-knowledge accuracy is near chance and that general ability is retained under the specified accuracy-and-chance criterion.
Tests fine-tuning on small subsets of the unlearning data, not unrelated or loosely related examples, nor recovery of each forgotten fact directly.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis showing that unlearning merely blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
Tests translations and jailbreak prompts, not ordinary paraphrase-only prompts or in-context information.
Tests TRU against cross-lingual, jailbreak, and relearning attacks; does not test resistance to quantization or internal edits, or establish resistance for all unlearning methods.

rows.subject: TRU (Zephyr-7B-beta)
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned with 15 samples from the unlearning dataset for one epoch (Relearning0).
rows.note: The text says UQ decreases only slightly and describes TRU as stable under relearning. UQ is the study's judged measure of removing undesired knowledge and controlling responses, not a direct fact-recall accuracy.
rows.check: Version codes were V2/V6; they map to B/F. UQ fell 7.01→6.56 (−0.45), a small move toward recovery, described as slight, with no uncertainty reported. UQ is a composite judge score, so the drop may partly reflect refusal style rather than knowledge. The attack is weak: 15 forget samples, 1 epoch.
